text: Remind me to message Tendai the evening before his half marathon on Sunday. He's been struggling with his knee since the Leeds 10k in September and is quite nervous about it. His physio said he should be fine if he keeps the pace steady, but he's convinced it'll go at mile nine like last time. Maybe suggest he walks the hills.
Lunch with Carmen. Her team is being restructured sometime next week and she's worried her manager, Patrick, will be moved to the Leeds office.
Fang has got really into Warhammer. He's painting a whole Ultramarines army and says he's done about forty models since the summer.
Dmitri and his wife Natasha are going to Lisbon for their tenth anniversary at the end of the month.
Need to pick up the dry cleaning before Friday and book the car in for its MOT sometime next week.
Sean mentioned his daughter Mia starts secondary school in early September. He seems more anxious about it than she is.
Call with the client went fine. Ibrahim Yilmaz is taking over the account from Thursday, so I should send him the handover notes tomorrow.
Joy supports Wrexham and has done since long before the Hollywood takeover. She's going to the away game at Bolton this weekend.
Helen's mum is having her hip replaced next Tuesday. Don't forget to text Helen the day after to see how it went.
Gabriel's leaving drinks were cancelled because half the office has flu. He finishes on Friday regardless.
Aisha knits constantly. She's making a cardigan for her sister Tamar's baby, who's due in early March.
Rohan had his promotion review yesterday. Haven't heard how it went yet, so I must ask him on Monday.
Note to self: Bridget is vegan and doesn't drink. Keep that in mind for the team dinner.
Pedro has a new puppy called Biscuit. Apparently it ate one of his climbing shoes last night.
Eamon is learning the fiddle and has his first session at the pub in a fortnight. He said he's terrified of playing in front of people.
I'm driving Joe to the airport on Saturday morning, so no plans before lunch.

Thomas says the new head of sales, a woman called Dorota Petrov, starts in two weeks. He thinks she'll shake things up a lot. She's coming from a competitor and has a reputation for scrapping targets and starting again from scratch, which is going to go down badly with Eamon's team, who only just hit theirs. Thomas seemed quietly pleased about it.
Sunil is coeliac, which I always forget. Also hates mushrooms.
Remind me to ring Uncle Tariq on Wednesday. It's his seventieth on Thursday and I won't be able to call on the day.

Fern has been off work since the miscarriage and isn't really answering messages. Her partner Juan said she's not doing great. I should drop round with some food this weekend, nothing fancy, and maybe check in with Juan as well sometime next week because he's clearly carrying a lot on his own.
Adaeze's book club is reading Piranesi this month. She thinks I'd love it and said I can borrow her copy when they've finished at the end of October.
Marisol got the job at the design studio! She starts on the 3rd of November.
Yaw's band are playing the Brudenell on Friday night. I've already got tickets for me and Sophie.
Aleksander's been signed off with stress. His boss keeps emailing him anyway. I need to check how he's doing later this week.
Spent ages talking to Natasha about crochet. She sells little amigurumi animals at the Christmas market every year and is already behind on stock.
Gift idea for Carmen: she keeps going on about a Kindle Paperwhite but won't buy one for herself.
Patrick's son Sam has his driving test next Thursday morning. Remind me to send Patrick a good luck message that evening, the night before.
Rohan is a massive Arsenal fan and has had a season ticket for twelve years. Never mention Spurs around him.
Ibrahim and his wife are expecting their second in the spring. He told me while we were waiting for the lift, so I don't think many people know yet.
Quick one: Tamar's moving flats at the end of the month, somewhere near Clapham. She asked if I could help carry boxes on the Saturday.

The quarterly review with Dmitri got moved to next Wednesday afternoon. Need to finish the slides by Tuesday and send them to Helen first for a sanity check. Dmitri wants the churn figures broken down by region this time, and he hates it when the numbers don't match the dashboard, so double check those against Ibrahim's report before anything goes out.
Joe's dad passed away on Sunday. The funeral is sometime next week, date not fixed yet. Remind me to send a card tomorrow and to ask Joe whether he'd like anyone from work there.
Sophie is training for the Great North Run. She's up to ten miles and is aiming for under two hours.
Juan plays five-a-side on Tuesdays and keeps asking me to join. Maybe after Christmas.
Bridget's daughter graduated from Edinburgh last week, first class in Geology. She was beaming showing me the photos.
Need to remember to renew my passport before early March. The trip is booked for the 20th.

Gabriel said the client in Rotterdam wants a site visit over the summer. He's asked if I want to go with him. Probably three days, flying from Manchester. Their operations director, Mr Moreau, is apparently very particular and likes everything printed, so worth bringing hard copies. Gabriel's been there twice and says the hotel by the port is the one to book.
Mia, Sean's daughter, apparently won the regional chess tournament last weekend. Should congratulate her next time I see them.
Thomas Walsh, or Tommo as everyone calls him, has been made redundant. His last day is the end of November. He's putting a brave face on it.

Talked to Eamon for ages about his model railway. He's building a layout of Dublin Connolly in his garage and is obsessed with getting the signals right. He showed me a video of a little train going through a tunnel he made from papier mache. Very wholesome. He's hoping to show it at the exhibition in Harrogate in the spring.
Yaw had his interview with the council on Monday. Must message him tomorrow to find out how it went, he seemed fairly confident.
Dorota's cat Pierogi needs an operation next Friday. She's beside herself about it.
Aisha and Pedro are getting married next summer! They haven't set a date yet but are looking at venues in Cornwall.

Sunil says his manager has been impossible lately and he's thinking about leaving. He's had a couple of interviews already, and there's a final round with a fintech in Shoreditch sometime next week. He's quite nervous because it involves a live coding test in front of three people. Remind me to message him the day before.
Book the restaurant for Saturday. Order flowers. Pay the gas bill.
Fang is starting a part-time MSc in data science in January while still working full time. Don't forget to ask him in a fortnight how the application went.
Natasha's brother Aleksander is coming over from Warsaw for Christmas. She hasn't seen him in three years.
Adaeze has her viva on the 14th. She's nervous but well prepared. Remind me to text her good luck the morning of, and then take her for a drink the week after to celebrate.
Joy mentioned she's been playing Baldur's Gate 3 every evening for a month. Says it's the best game she's ever played.
Called Mrs Johnson about the parish newsletter. She wants my piece by Thursday at the latest.
Carmen's anniversary is next Tuesday and her husband has forgotten every year so far. She's dropping heavy hints about a weekend away in the Cotswolds.
Tendai finished the half marathon in 1:52! Really pleased for him. Knee held up fine.
Helen and her partner Marisol are hosting a housewarming on Saturday the 8th. I'm bringing dessert.
Patrick is a serious birdwatcher. He went to Norfolk last weekend specifically to see a rare warbler and missed it by ten minutes.

Tariq's surgery has been pushed back again, now sometime early next month. He's fed up with the waiting and can barely walk to the shop now. His wife has had to take time off to drive him to appointments, and their son Rohan is up from London most weekends to help. I should ring him over the weekend and see how he's coping.

Fern Popescu from accounts is leaving at the end of the year to go travelling round South America. She's going to Peru first, then Bolivia, and wants to finish in Patagonia sometime in March. She's been saving for four years. Her partner isn't going, which sounds like it's been a bit of a sore point at home. Someone should organise a collection for her before she goes.
Sean's wife Bridget has her scan on Friday. He's going with her but seemed a bit on edge.
Nothing much to note. Long day.
Gabriel recommended a podcast about the history of the Premier League. Should listen on the train.

Dmitri's daughter turns sixteen next Saturday and he's throwing a surprise party. He wants ideas for a present; she's into vinyl and Fleetwood Mac. Remind me to send him the link to that record shop in Leeds tomorrow, and then check the week after how the party went.
